claims.text: As-fabricated high-entropy-alloy components exhibit residual stress.
As-fabricated high-entropy-alloy components exhibit porosity.
Non-uniform thermal gradients cause dimensional distortion in as-fabricated high-entropy-alloy components.
An integrated enhanced cooling system combined with adjusted laser power and scanning parameters can better control thermal gradients during laser powder bed fusion.
The intervention will improve microstructural uniformity.
The intervention will reduce residual stresses.
The intervention will decrease porosity formation.
Enhanced cooling extracts heat more uniformly during laser powder bed fusion.
Enhanced cooling accelerates and homogenizes solidification.
More uniform heat extraction minimizes thermal gradients.
Minimizing thermal gradients reduces porosity and residual stress.
Reduced porosity and residual stress improve dimensional precision.
Reduced porosity and residual stress improve mechanical integrity.
Relative to conventional laser powder bed fusion, the intervention will moderately reduce defect density.
Relative to conventional laser powder bed fusion, the intervention will improve repeatability of dimensional tolerances.
Relative to conventional laser powder bed fusion, the intervention will improve mechanical strength.
Conventional laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys typically produces thermal-gradient-induced residual stresses and porosity.
The benefits will be less pronounced for very large or complex builds and for additive-manufacturing methods other than laser powder bed fusion.
The magnitude of improvement will vary with alloy composition and build geometry.
Failure to achieve statistically significant improvements in dimensional precision, residual stress, and porosity relative to a conventional-process control will falsify the hypothesis.
